newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end weaker but above day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end weaker but above day's lows.

text.p: Manila blue chips ended a lacklustre session weaker, but shares recouped some ground by the closing bell.
Concerns about interest rate direction here and abroad capped investor interest as did seasonal weakness ahead of Holy Week, traders said. But some mid-cap issues captured interest.
"People are top-slicing many of their big caps," said Louie Bate, managing director at ING Barings Securities. But, he added, "the mid-caps are holding".
After dipping to as low as 3193.50, the composite index ended off 0.50 percent or 16.22 points to 3215.64.

Teresa Lee of Asia Merit Securities Inc said the stock market was hampered by "many factors" including jitters about an ongoing insider trading probe at the stock exchange and the absence of foreign investors.
Jonas Ferrer, a vice president at Pryce Securities Inc, said the decline in Philippine interest rates is raising concerns that foreign funds may seek higher returns in other markets.
"If there is a small difference in interest rates, people will go to a market with less risk," he said.
Sugar miller Victorias Milling dropped 50 centavos to 4.10 pesos on news its creditors are yet to receive disbursals of interest payments it made last Friday, traders said.
